ready1_open_rewrite.title: SciVerse open question
ready1_open_rewrite.rewritten_question_text: The Michaelis equation is expressed in the form $y=\frac{V_\mathrm{max}[S]}{K_\mathrm{m}+[S]}$, where $y$ represents the reaction rate, $V_\mathrm{max}$ represents the maximum reaction rate, $[S]$ represents the substrate concentration, and $K_\mathrm{m}$ represents the Michaelis constant. When a competitive inhibitor is added to the reaction system, $V_\mathrm{max}$ remains unchanged, but the value of $K_\mathrm{m}$ will increase.

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: the image gives the double-reciprocal straight-line form of the Michaelis equation: 1/V = (Km/Vmax)·(1/[S]) + 1/Vmax. Among them, the y-intercept term is 1/Vmax, and the slope term is Km/Vmax, therefore Km is reflected in the slope, and Vmax is reflected in the intercept. Then reason: when a competitive inhibitor is added, the Vmax of the enzymatic reaction remains unchanged, but the apparent Km increases. Since Vmax remains unchanged while Km increases, the direction of change of Km is increase.

method.method_draft: First describe the displayed equation: the graphing form shows Vmax in the intercept term and Km in the slope term. From the text, competitive inhibitor is added. Apply the competitive-inhibition rule that Vmax is unchanged while apparent Km becomes larger. Therefore the requested change in Km is an increase.
method.CoT_raw: 先描述图像：图像中给出米氏方程的双倒数直线形式：1/V = (Km/Vmax)·(1/[S]) + 1/Vmax。其中纵截距项是 1/Vmax，斜率项是 Km/Vmax，因此 Km 体现在斜率中，Vmax 体现在截距中。再推理：加入竞争性抑制剂时，酶促反应的 Vmax 保持不变，但表观 Km 增大。由于 Vmax 不变而 Km 增大，Km 的变化方向就是增大。

planner_metadata.distinctiveness_rationale: Directly uses the visualized double-reciprocal form to connect competitive inhibition to the parameter affected; this is the natural single route for the problem.
planner_metadata.image_role: Read the image as the Lineweaver–Burk form of the Michaelis–Menten equation: 1/V = (Km/Vmax)(1/[S]) + 1/Vmax, where the y-intercept depends on 1/Vmax and the slope depends on Km/Vmax.
planner_metadata.text_role: Use the question text to identify the situation as addition of a competitive inhibitor and to confirm the variables in the Michaelis–Menten equation, especially that Km is the Michaelis constant being asked about.
planner_metadata.knowledge_role: Use the enzyme-kinetics rule for competitive inhibition: inhibitor competes with substrate at the active site, so sufficiently high substrate can still reach the same Vmax, but the apparent Km increases because more substrate is needed to reach half-maximal velocity.
